newsitem.title: DENMARK: ISS sold U.S. unit for modest sum-Schmidt.
newsitem.headline: ISS sold U.S. unit for modest sum-Schmidt.

text.p: Danish cleaning group International Service System (ISS) said on Wednesday it sold its troubled United States ISS Inc unit to Canada's Aaxis for a modest sum but did not divulge the actual price.
"It is a rather modest sum. The analysts' estimates just don't hold," ISS chief executive Waldemar Schmidt told Reuters in a telephone call.
"We had originally expected a better price. The deal is nonetheless in the best interests of ISS shareholders," he said.
Earlier ISS announced that it signed a purchase deal with Canada's Aaxis Ltd on the sale of its U.S. unit ISS inc.
In August, ISS issued first-half 1996 results showing a two billion crown loss caused by falsified accounts in ISS Inc.
Last August the two firms signed a letter of intent on the sale of ISS International Service System System Inc, the troubled ISS US unit, to Montreal bourse-listed Aaxis Limited.
No price for the deal was mentioned but Danish analysts have previously estimated ISS Inc's sale value at between 400-800 million crowns. --Per Bech Thomsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
